Nos. 17-1717 and 18-18 

In the Supreme Court of the United States 

THE AMERICAN LEGION, ET AL., PETITIONERS 

v.  

AMERICAN HUMANIST ASSOCIATION, ET AL.  

MARYLAND-NATIONAL CAPITAL PARK AND PLANNING 
COMMISSION, PETITIONER 

AMERICAN HUMANIST ASSOCIATION, ET AL.  

v.  

On Writs of Certiorari  
to the United States Court of Appeals for the Fourth Circuit  

UNOPPOSED APPLICATION OF RESPONDENTS FOR LEAVE TO FILE A 
CONSOLIDATED BRIEF ON THE MERITS IN EXCESS OF THE WORD LIMIT 

MONICA L. MILLER 
      Counsel of Record 
AMERICAN HUMANIST ASSOCIATION 
1821 Jefferson Place N.W. 
Washington, D.C. 20036 
(202) 238-9088 
mmiller@americanhumanist.org 
Counsel for Respondents

Respondents respectfully request leave to file a single consolidated brief on the 

merits in excess of the word limit for a single brief set forth in Supreme Court Rule 

33(d), not to exceed 22,500 words. Petitioners have consented to this request.  

1. 

On November 2, 2018, the Court entered an order consolidating Docket 

Nos. 17-1717 and 18-18.  

2. 

Petitioner The American Legion, et al. (as Intervenors) and Petitioner 

Maryland-National  Capital  Park  and  Planning  Commission  (as  Defendant),  filed 

separate briefs on the merits with a combined total word limit of 30,000 words.  

3. 

Rather  than  file  two  separate  response  briefs  on  the  merits, 

Respondents believe it will be more efficient and beneficial to the Court and parties 

to file a single consolidated response brief on the merits.   

4. 

Respondents respectfully request permission to file a consolidated brief 

in excess of the 15,000-word limit by 7,500 words, not to exceed 22,500 words total.  

5. 

6. 

Counsel for both Petitioners have assented to the relief sought herein.  

This  request  is  sought  in  the  interest  of  justice,  not  for  delay,  and  no 

party will be prejudiced if the requested word extension is granted. 

The application for leave to file a consolidated response brief on the merits of 

22,500 words should be granted. 

Respectfully submitted, 

Monica L. Miller  
     Counsel of Record 
American Humanist Association 

1

1821 Jefferson Place NW  
Washington, DC 20036  
mmiller@americanhumanist.org 

Counsel for Respondents  

 December 17, 2018 

2
